newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria permits hard currency bank accounts.
newsitem.headline: Syria permits hard currency bank accounts.

text.p: Syrians can now open hard currency bank accounts without having to disclose the source of their funds, banking sources and government officials said.
A new government decree effective from Wednesday allows hard currency accounts which pay five percent interest if funds are deposited for more than three months.
Officials said the decree would pave the way for the return to Syria of millions of dollars of Syrian money currently being deposited in banks in neighbouring Lebanon and Jordan.

The decree allows hard currency to be transferred abroad provided it is used for medical treatment, education, or payment for books, newspaper subscriptions and similar non-commercial purposes, the decree said.

Banking souces said that within the next few days the central bank will adjust the rate of the Syrian pound from 42 to the U.S. dollar to between 43 and 44 pounds, as part of government efforts to narrow the gap with the black market rate of 48 to 50 pounds.
The rate of 42 to a dollar, called the encouragement or the parallel rate, is currently applied to over 80 percent of dealings in Syria.

There is also an official rate of 11.2 pounds to a dollar which is used for a very limited number of transactions, and a customs rate of 23 pounds to a dollar which is used to calculate customs duties.
Economic analysts said the government is still proceeding with its plans to unify the rates close to the real value of the pound.
